title: Discriminative Accuracy of Plasma Phospho-tau217 for Alzheimer Disease vs Other Neurodegenerative Disorders
themes: Early detection in familial Alzheimer's disease
one_line: Plasma P-tau217 is a highly accurate blood biomarker capable of distinguishing Alzheimer's disease from other neurodegenerative disorders and identifying pathology decades before symptom onset.
summary: This cross-sectional study evaluated the diagnostic accuracy of plasma P-tau217 for Alzheimer's disease across three diverse cohorts totaling 1,402 participants. The groups included an Arizona-based neuropathology cohort, the Swedish BioFINDER-2 clinical cohort, and a Colombian autosomal-dominant AD kindred (PSEN1 E280A). The study found that plasma P-tau217 accurately discriminated Alzheimer's disease from other neurodegenerative diseases with high accuracy (AUCs ranging from 0.89 to 0.96). This performance was significantly better than other plasma biomarkers like P-tau181 and NfL, as well as MRI measures, and was statistically comparable to established CSF and PET biomarkers. Additionally, plasma P-tau217 levels were significantly elevated in familial mutation carriers roughly 20 years before the estimated onset of mild cognitive impairment.

key_claims.claim: Plasma P-tau217 differentiates neuropathologically defined Alzheimer's disease from non-AD with significantly higher accuracy than plasma P-tau181 and NfL.
key_claims.evidence: In cohort 1, the AUC was 0.89 (95% CI, 0.81-0.97) for P-tau217, compared to an AUC range of 0.50-0.72 for P-tau181 and NfL (P < .05).

key_claims.claim: Plasma P-tau217 discriminates clinical AD dementia from other neurodegenerative diseases better than MRI and other plasma markers, and comparably to CSF and PET measures.
key_claims.evidence: In cohort 2, the AUC was 0.96 for P-tau217 versus 0.50-0.81 for plasma P-tau181, NfL, and MRI (P < .001); there was no significant difference compared with CSF P-tau217, CSF P-tau181, and tau-PET (AUC range, 0.90-0.99; P > .15).

key_claims.claim: Plasma P-tau217 levels are elevated decades before the onset of cognitive symptoms in familial Alzheimer's disease.
key_claims.evidence: In cohort 3 (PSEN1 E280A carriers), P-tau217 levels were significantly greater among mutation carriers from approximately 25 years of age and older, which is 20 years prior to estimated onset of MCI.

key_claims.claim: Plasma P-tau217 levels correlate with tau tangles only in the presence of β-amyloid plaques.
key_claims.evidence: In cohort 1, plasma P-tau217 correlated with tau tangles in participants with β-amyloid plaques (Spearman ρ = 0.64; P < .001) but not in those without plaques (Spearman ρ = 0.15; P = .33).

methods.population: Three cohorts: an Arizona neuropathology cohort (n=81), the Swedish BioFINDER-2 clinical cohort (n=699), and a Colombian autosomal-dominant AD kindred (n=622).

limitations: Findings require validation in unselected and diverse populations.
The plasma P-tau217 assay needs further optimization to determine its potential role in clinical care.
The cross-sectional study design limits inferences regarding longitudinal changes.

issues: Missing front-matter metadata entirely (affiliations, corresponding author, emails).
